# Deep research brief: Sound -> light for concerts/festivals, TRAINED ON DANCE datasets (LightSem v2): generative audio -> light on dance-derived targets
## Problem state
Accepted representation-first implementation 2026-09-10. Build convincing music-driven stage lighting. Music is the only playback input; an internal generated skeleton/motion sequence is explicitly allowed. Hybrid measured audio dynamics may control brightness and movement intensity. Quiet passages must remain visible but restrained. Establish clean motion-source and temporal-codec quality before audio training. Prior human review rejects flashing/juggling reconstructions and excessive Shpongle movement; only the incumbent audio-to-descriptions-to-pose path is currently visually convincing. Glare improvement is useful but does not establish visible head-brightness dynamics. Exploration seed0; confirm only qualifying finalist and matched baseline at seed1. Accelerated BF16/compile/prefetch in matched arms, no earlier 2–3h ceiling. Historical nulls and gates remain valid.
Primary diagnostic: `descriptor-audio-r2-over-identity` (no declared target).
Current synthesis:
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Local evidence: repeated tuning of stems, frozen audio features, model size, per-bar level regression, six-moment group decoding and critic/cue recipes did not close the designed-appearance gap. Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

Human pilot:39ratings, one rater,29registered song groups. Held-out preference-model accuracy56.4%/59.0% with intervals including chance; music accuracy equals its majority-side baseline and appearance logloss0.739 is worse than0.693 chance. Fresh generated-candidate-vs-default wins are unmeasured. These ratings do not test new GroupEngine wave/colour controls. Median screen-luma mismatch16.1%; the blinder metric squares dimmer while the renderer is linear. Preserve old data/scores, version the correction, verify canonical audio identity and material matching before fresh preference claims.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. Transfer to LightSem is untested. Glow with the Flow itself reports that synchronization/congruence ratings miss repetition and colour-richness defects. SeqLight weight release is not verified. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

Next experiments, in order of dependencies: material/metric validation; isolated beat benchmark; explicit recurrence-memory vs equally varied no-memory composition; active vs random pair acquisition; histogram/assignment oracle followed only conditionally by matched audio-conditioned training; independently reviewed authored-look oracle to measure renderer/planner capability. Budgets and thresholds in the report are proposals, not preregistrations. Confirm primary outcomes, independence unit and gates before execution; do not interpret an oracle failure as a uniquely identified cause.

No new training/rendering/GPU job or experiment closure was performed in this review. Additional Just Dance extraction remains a separate process; freeze and audit completed features before using new data. Existing interpretation debt and statuses are not cleared by this synthesis. Sources and detailed report: /root/lightsem/docs/research/2026-09-08/LightSem_Research_Review_2026-09-08.pdf; local evidence /root/lightsem/docs/CONTINUATION_AUDIT_2026-09-07.md and /root/lightsem/docs/HL_RATINGS_2026-09-08.md.
## Already tried and DEAD under the current recipe (do NOT re-propose)
- [refuted] A causal Conformer with three heads — deterministic block A, event hazard block B, conditional-flow block C — trained on AIST++ produces light that lands on the music like dance-derived light does, wi (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Two fixes follow from the mechanism, and neither is 'train longer'. First, the block A / block C boundary was drawn from the literature and should be redrawn from the Stage 0b audit: on this corpus almost nothing clears the identity baseline, so almost everything belongs in the SAMPLED block, not the regressed one. Regressing an unpredictable channel does not produce a cautious estimate, it produces a flat line, and a flat line makes bad light. Second, the flow head samples each frame independently given the trunk state, so its variety is high-frequency jitter rather than the burst-and-rest structure real dance has; it needs to condition on its own previous output. Both are v2 work. Meanwhile the diagnostic to keep is the one that caught this: report the event RATE and the circular-shift null next to every Light-BAS, because a model can raise alignment and lose the comparison by flashing more.
- [inconclusive] A factorised audio-light critic trained with time-shift, other-song AND beat-trigger negatives on bar-synchronous tokens learns something beyond beat and loudness: it separates real authored light fro
- [refuted] A learned group-effects decoder (Anton's mixture of light: a shared type-masked head on the frozen trunk and operator head emitting per-group intensity envelope, palette, effect id, rate in beats, pha
- [inconclusive] A look sampler that HOLDS its sampled look between cues fired by the calibrated look-change hazard (refractory 2 s, rate matched to the corpus) reproduces the authored corpora's look-transition statis
- [inconclusive] Authored hobby/game light shows are lighting corpora, not tempo corpora: on xLights free .xsq sequences (where the song is on disk) and Beat Saber lightshow maps, audio predicts the group-level event 
- [refuted] Conditioning on whole-track structure -- section label and time to the next drop -- is worth more than anything else the offline setting buys, because structure is where the largest measured effect in
- [inconclusive] Dance is not a category error for light. Light derived from real dance motion through the hybrid conductor (dance envelopes, audio-phased transients), brightness-matched against a 30-line audio beat t
- [inconclusive] Feeding the group decoder the hazard features of its OWN emitted cues (teacher-forced in training, autoregressive in 1 s blocks at inference) raises its held-out cue-timing lift above the audio-only d
- [inconclusive] A beat-conditioned A/B/C sequence model with correct world aiming and independent emitted-light checks will produce more physically valid visible movement than the current no-clock body-v2 prototype w (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: World-target geometry repairs emitted-light visibility (1.0 vs 0.0); old weights with the same map also reach 1.0. The new recipe does not establish musical motion control: only 0.025 of40songs pass same-beat spectral-response/noise criteria, and A alignment advantage is -0.2130; report event selectivity's separate pass without hiding these failures. A future motion-control change must be evaluated on emitted trajectories with fixed rhythm and paired noise, retaining local timing checks.
- [inconclusive] Higher declared simulated actuator limits restore more fast motion under the same full-track convex target-fitting objective.
- [inconclusive] Explicit clean-estimate FK/support/root objectives reduce generated sliding on held-out native motion versus a matched masked-native flow baseline without losing independent quality or conditioning ga
- [inconclusive] Full-track convex angular fitting reduces requested-to-emitted delay while preserving hard quantized mechanics.
- [inconclusive] Turn-separated bounded regional geometry and a floor/back-wall chart prevent the recorded contraction while retaining changing surface trajectories.
- [inconclusive] Explicit signed root-up lean restores projected torso movement omitted by turn-separated regional mapping while retaining separate bounded lanes.
- [inconclusive] Offline zero-phase target smoothing and angular velocity feedforward reduce delay of saved requested gestures under unchanged quantized hard mechanics.
- [inconclusive] A temporal continuous motion codec preserves clean dance dynamics better than a framewise 24-channel encoder. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: This codec recipe retains recognizable poses but fails dynamics, physical contact and/or full-track fidelity. Root-relative diagnostics are needed because fixing accumulated root drift alone may not repair limb velocity. Do not start music training from an ineligible representation; freeze a distinct revision with direct short-hold coverage.
- [inconclusive] Shared body choreography and bounded regional expression reduce excessive rig movement while retaining active choreography. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Shared articulated targets, quantified mechanical limits and direct measured loudness separate useful lighting behavior from generator quality. A downstream improvement cannot reverse weak conditionality or physical-motion failure upstream.
- [inconclusive] Direct audio loudness controls improve visible quiet-to-entry brightness contrast without losing quiet-stage visibility. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Shared articulated targets, quantified mechanical limits and direct measured loudness separate useful lighting behavior from generator quality. A downstream improvement cannot reverse weak conditionality or physical-motion failure upstream.
- [inconclusive] Fixed calibrated exposure restores visible dimmer response compressed by time-varying total-intensity normalization. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: One shared fixed exposure does not simultaneously retain single-beam visibility and whole-rig response under identical per-kind radiance gains. Fixed role calibration is a distinct intervention; a future primary must be fixed before outcomes even if a selection gate fails.
- [refuted] More accurate integration of the incumbent flow reduces excess high-frequency pose motion while retaining active movement. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Increasing integration steps alone did not meet the preregistered jitter-improvement and preservation gates; the learned motion/decoder remains a separate issue.
- [inconclusive] A conditional temporal flow on full native motion uses the correct music and preserves coherent dynamics better than a matched deterministic regressor. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Learning the marginal motion distribution and reducing energy score versus a regressor do not establish music timing. Physical foot constraints are missing from the native quadratic objective; contact labels remain populated while feet slide. Global chunk consistency does not bound generated root travel. Preserve this failed recipe and freeze a distinct targeted revision.
- [refuted] A phase-preserving linear codec with explicit root/contact channels can satisfy clean-motion fidelity gates where the 20k nonlinear temporal codec recipe failed. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Pose accuracy alone hides severe temporal distortion from bandwise truncation. Even the largest candidate fails velocity, kinetic energy, planted feet and short-hold gates. Retain full native detail as an explicit uncompressed engineering reference before music generation; do not call it learned compression success.
- [inconclusive] Surface-space regional mapping removes persistent illumination collapse and retains changing separated trajectories on the saved Shpongle motion. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Surface-space targets remove the persistent central focus caused by elevated inward targets. Articulation bandwidth and a complete changing composition are separate gates; spatial spread alone is not dancing to music. Both present restrained broad columns with modest differences; not convincing recovered choreography. Active total/relative extent and active median speed fail frozen bars. No continuous audiovisual or human acceptance claimed.
- [inconclusive] Recovering attenuated articulation bandwidth increases changing separated surface trajectories without reintroducing collapse or excessive speed on the saved Shpongle motion. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Surface-space targets remove the persistent central focus caused by elevated inward targets. Articulation bandwidth and a complete changing composition are separate gates; spatial spread alone is not dancing to music. All555 half-second frames inspected. Substantial changing separated motion and floor sweeps replace the always-central knot, but the visible composition still mainly uses the same floor-facing crown/fan. Local visual reconvergence around194-201s remains; the strict4-axis1.5m focus duration understates this perceived interval. Do not declare a complete dancing-light fix from track-average gates or these sampled images. Music fit and human acceptance unmeasured.
- [inconclusive] The fixed group-expression adapter yields expressive dimmers and distinguishable conditional fixture groups while preserving mirror geometry and visibility. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: The same incumbent checkpoint isolates the adapter change from retraining. Several conditional draws and a fixed geometric/brightness policy are not a learned fixture-level lighting director; engineering gate outcomes do not override failed musical-control gates or establish human aesthetic preference.
- [inconclusive] Repeated audio FiLM in the temporal flow increases meaningful audio control relative to single-entry conditioning. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Repeated FiLM changes how audio enters each flow block and adds parameters; the matched factorial comparison tests this recipe rather than a pure parameter-count intervention. Swap response must be accompanied by correct-audio alignment and preserved native/output quality.
- [inconclusive] Local Fourier coordinates of the existing spectral-flux streams improve music-conditioned motion generation. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Inspect every matched fourier/Base comparison across both architectures and seeds. A lower joint trajectory score alone does not establish musical correspondence, local embedding use, expressive brightness or product acceptance; all frozen gates and supplementary controls are reported separately.
- [inconclusive] BF16 and benchmark-selected runtime optimizations at matched sample exposure reduce complete training time by at least2x while retaining quality within3% for base_once and muq_film in both seeds. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Native BF16 plus compiled execution and prefetch cuts this four-cell workload by about5.26x, but the combined recipe does not earn the3%noninferiority/output gate: base comparisons remain imprecise, while MuQ loses screen-light qualification and one AP point estimate exceeds3%. Keep FP32 defaults; isolate BF16 from compilation and its different dropout execution in any newly registered follow-up rather than retrying this bundle.
- [refuted] The pinned released MuQ representation improves native conditional motion beyond the92-feature baseline. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: Inspect every matched muq/Base comparison across both architectures and seeds. A lower joint trajectory score alone does not establish musical correspondence, local embedding use, expressive brightness or product acceptance; all frozen gates and supplementary controls are reported separately.
- [refuted] Local periodicity recovers annotated beats better than the incumbent constant tempo grid. (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: The fixed PLP recipe underperforms the constant grid on this358-clip GuitarSet benchmark despite succeeding on some synthetic tempo changes. Keep local periodicity as a representation/control question; do not replace the rhythm tracker on this evidence or generalize the failure to all local methods.
- [inconclusive] Adding the verified new Just Dance training recordings, under the repaired common protocol, improves within-song 2-second com_speed/vert_bounce_amp R2 by at least0.02 over old-only training across fiv (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: With the repaired descriptor recipe and fixed 12,000-update budget, adding 208 eligible JD recordings/345 coaches produced only +0.01098 canonical-song R², with a wide interval spanning zero; both old and expanded models remained negative on newly acquired songs. This does not establish the +0.02 claim or a general failure of additional data, and the motion test remains sealed. Repeating the same recipe to seek favorable seeds is not justified; a follow-up should first identify a substantive target, supervision or optimization change and preregister its comparison.
- [inconclusive] Just Dance coach motion is predictable from audio on held-out songs in a way AIST++ motion was not, because the choreography is made to the song's structure rather than improvised to a structure-less 
- [refuted] Light derived from real dance motion by a fixed body-following mapping (conductor v0) is musically timed: its visible accents align to the beat better than the same accents circularly shifted, and the (failure_mode: mechanism_wrong) — lesson: The idea survives, the assumed mechanism does not. The hypothesis assumed a dancing body carries the musics timing into the light. It carries the PERIOD (footfall Rayleigh R 0.55, median z 5.2 per clip) but not the PHASE, which belongs to the choreography and is therefore not in the audio and not learnable from it. Dance supplies WHAT the light does (how much, how wide, which side, how deep the bounce, when the look changes); audio supplies WHEN the transients land. Evidence that this is a fix and not a retreat: the hybrid conductor built on that split scores +0.124 (CI [+0.114,+0.135]) against +0.094 (CI [+0.083,+0.106]) for the audio-only beat trigger, while staying close to the dance-derived look (FID 43 to the oracle vs 794 to the beat trigger). Stage 1 trains block A as regression on dance-derived envelopes and block B as a hazard conditioned on audio beat phase, never an absolute event phase copied from the dancer. Stage 0c must compare the HYBRID against the beat trigger, brightness-matched; comparing the motion-only oracle would test a straw man this experiment already shows is mistimed.
- [refuted] Most of the gap between the model's light (+0.018 against its null) and light mapped from the real dance (+0.211) is caused by the causality constraint, not by the corpus. The same trunk with unmasked (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: The ceiling test did its job in one run: with the entire track visible, symmetric context and the offline bus, held-out block A R2 does not move and the light gates do not move, on AIST++. So the gap between model light and real-mapped light is not a causality tax and not a context-length problem; it is the corpus (Stage 0b: AIST++ movement is explained by genre, not audio). Three architecture experiments would have confirmed this slowly. Consequence: H-C (structure conditioning) is tested on Just Dance, where songs have structure, not on AIST++; and the pre-rendered path's honest advantages are H-B's lag removal and H-C/H-D anticipation, not accuracy.
- [inconclusive] One frozen music-foundation layer group (MuQ layers 9-12 or MERT-330M layers 10-13, plus MERT ~15-16 for rhythm), PCA'd to 32-64 d and dumped offline, carries lighting-relevant information the 92-chan
- [inconclusive] Section-level intent belongs on the conductor, not in the per-frame model: an audio-only offline planner that writes scene family, palette, intensity class, strobe density and transition type per sect
- [inconclusive] Source-separated stems add lighting-relevant information the 92-channel mix bus collapses: HTDemucs drums/bass/vocals/other envelopes, onsets and 2-band flux raise held-out event AP on the Just Dance 
- [inconclusive] The Just Dance background, with coach and UI masked, is a designed light show whose scene changes and palette shifts are predictable from audio in the same way a human operator's are on RPMC-L2: audio

- [refuted] The music-induced-movement literature's shared skeleton is present in AIST++: causal audio predicts the across-dancer mean of quantity of motion, vertical bounce amplitude, head speed and the embodied (failure_mode: recipe_conditional) — lesson: The recipe is conditional on the corpus. Dance-derived supervision only carries audio information when the music is the only thing that varies; in a choreographed corpus the choreography carries it instead. ## Ruled out by direct measurement (do NOT re-litigate)
- AIST++ can supply block A, the shared audio->movement skeleton. ELIMINATED for this corpus. What varies between AIST++ tracks is the dance GENRE, not the acoustics, and the movement follows the genre. (method: Direct replication of Burger et al. 2013's stimulus-level design on all 60 AIST++ tracks: one row per track, movement av)
- AIST++ needs a per-track audio-motion sync offset: the dance is period-locked but phase-random against the music because each track's motion clock is shifted by an unknown constant. ELIMINATED. (method: Fit one offset per music id as the R-weighted circular mean of per-clip footfall beat phases, using only half of each tr)
